body:
Native ledger patterns now execute through the production Census Gate. All six
matcher kinds classify hits as HOME, VARIANT or COPY, retain physical ownership,
and report stale declarations or unsupported contexts actionably.

Workspace aliases and reexports use Source definition sites and actual reading
modules. A shared code-context API preserves edition-specific code/import heads,
target identity and the original load allowance. Lexical scopes account for
parameters, local bindings, constants, imports and qualified syntax. Token and
literal matching reuse the existing normalizer/parser and PurRDF's bounded ECMA
implementation; normal form 1 and its fingerprints remain unchanged.
Import namespace checks follow expanded targets in their declaration frames,
with bounded dependency work and explicit cycle refusal. Younger scopes cannot
rewrite an outer import; direct shadows and inner reimports remain authoritative.
Literal matching excludes documentation-comment prose while retaining explicit
doc attributes. Native source ownership queries are shared by byte across
patterns and constant observations through PurRDF's fallible `OrderedTable`.
Lookup/update work is logarithmic; native arena growth and retained reference
capacity spend the original matching grant. A 4,000-binding fixture preserves
positive and clean-neighbor verdicts under the unchanged default grant.

Runnable memory-backed examples demonstrate code/import contexts and canonical
RDF policy construction. Capability documents and native assessments state the
supported contract and its refusal boundaries. Unindexed external spellings are
syntax observations; reference scanning and preferred-provider enforcement keep
their existing unavailable-execution refusals.

The Windows CI job is disabled under the maintainer's explicit instruction:
"Please disable CI windows tests on your next PR. For now, ignore those CI
results." Linux/macOS CI and required local cross-target compilation remain.
Windows execution is unverified.

Progresses #5. The parent remains open for its remaining detector, reference,
provider and default-goal acceptance.

Validation: the full `make check` passed on 1841a757. Corrected head af8b27a
passed all 60 production Gate cases, 24 Census library cases, affected Census/CLI package tests and
doctests, workspace all-target lint, and MSRV 1.98.1 workspace/fuzz checks.
The native changes completed and normal signed commit hooks passed. The
unchanged Source count fixture and all three local Source cross-target checks
retain their qualification from 003de42 after the count accessor. An
independent changed-finding review closed the transitive/declaration-frame
misses; compiler witnesses and positive/negative controls are retained.
Forge feedback on documentation comments and repeated ownership scans is
addressed with paired functional and resource-grant fixtures. The subsequent
quadratic cache lookup finding is fixed using the existing pinned native table,
with admission/error fixtures and focused independent review. Native Windows
bindings record not-applicable under observed Linux cfg; they are not runtime
passes.
Unchanged Source release/cross-target and five fuzz execution paths retain the
full-run qualification. The warnings-denied documentation build passed; this is
composite gate evidence, not a second full `make check` on the corrected head.

crates/raf-census/src/gate/patterns/paths.rs: 1
`151-160`: **🚀 Performance & Scalability** | **🔵 Trivial** | **⚡ Quick win** **Cache source owners per byte instead of scanning the file for each occurrence.** `source_owners` calls `workspace.item_at`, which filters every item of the file. It then calls `same_source` for each candidate. Several paths reach this function: - `matches` calls it for each path occurrence, and once more for each compiled pattern at that occurrence (`visit.rs` line 139 onward). - `constant` calls it for every pattern binding through `Paths::bind`. - `constant` also calls it for every `PatIdent` when a `path` pattern exists. The total cost grows with occurrences × items in the file × patterns. The `MatchLimits` step grant does not charge this work, so the limit does not bound the time on large generated files. Compute the owners once per file, for example from a sorted span index. Alternatively, memoize them by `site.byte` in the `Paths` visitor and pass the result into `matches` and `constant`. Based on learnings: "flag code that performs a linear scan over the full list for each item, causing O(n*m) behavior on large inputs. Prefer precomputing an index".
